answer: Securing an agent economy against Sybil attacks requires tying identity generation to scarce verifiable resources, anchoring virtual entities to physical realities much like mooring a ship at a fortified wharf. By demanding cryptographic proofs of specialized hardware execution—akin to validating a node atop an isolated mesa—networks can impose prohibitive capital expenditure. Furthermore, staking collateral through decentralized protocols such as willow ensures that any malicious spawning of fake AI agents incurs immediate economic forfeiture, neutralizing exploit profitability.
